reuse.why: Introduces getExpectedAmount on top of the existing getRangedAmount and the shared getApproxNumberThreshold, and routes getScheduledAmount and most server sites through it; but computeSchedulePreviewTransactions in the same file keeps its own number/range dispatch over getRangedAmount.

duplication.why: Removes three inline 'null ? 0 : number ? value : getRangedAmount' dispatches, but leaves the same dispatch in computeSchedulePreviewTransactions and keeps a separate op ternary in schedule-template around the new helper.

placement.why: The rule is in shared/schedules.ts next to getRangedAmount/getScheduledAmount, reusing the tolerance function from shared/rules.

scope.why: Only the amount-resolution sites, the new helper, tests and a release note are touched.

maintainability.why: The op is an optional trailing parameter, so the preview path and the desktop getScheduledAmount callers (SchedulesTable, Balance, mobile lists, useScheduleEdit) silently keep the old rule for approximate amounts; whether the rule applies depends on each caller remembering to pass op.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions still resolves the amount with its own typeof/getRangedAmount dispatch instead of getExpectedAmount, so previews ignore the approximate rule.

disguised_duplication.where: The remaining copies (preview dispatch in computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, op ternary in schedule-template createScheduleList) are left visibly as they were, not reshaped.

one_place.where: The rule lands in getExpectedAmount, but computeSchedulePreviewTransactions does not call it and the desktop-client getScheduledAmount callers do not pass op, so those paths keep the exact value for approximate amounts.
